newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt and futures stuck in narrow ranges.
newsitem.headline: German debt and futures stuck in narrow ranges.

text.p: German bunds and futures were slightly lower in lacklustre late dealings on Monday as the market remained stuck in ranges with few fresh fundamentals to influence dealings, traders said.
DTB June Bund futuers were down 14 basis points at 100.31 after breaking support at 100.35 but lacked volumes to push the contract lower despite lower U.S. debt market prices.
The benchmark 10-year 6.00 percent Bund due January 2007 was trading at 100.59, down from 100.72 at the end of Friday.
Market activities, however, were expected to pick up on Tuesday with a fresh batch of U.S. economic data.

While only German current accounts data is expected on Tuesday, the market will focus on the release of durable goods orders for March and the April consumer confidence index for any signs of inflation pressure.
Also scheduled for Tuesday is the U.S. first quarter employment cost index.

Any mounting speculation about a U.S. interest rate hike after the reports would likely weigh on the German market as well despite few concerns about German inflation but the domestic outlook would be a mitigating factor, traders said.
